type alias.description:
TS 1.4
type Name = ...
Gives an existing type (primitive, union, object shape, etc.) a new name. Unlike `interface`, a type alias can't be reopened/merged, but can name unions, tuples, and other non-object types.

union type.description:
TS 1.4
type Name = A | B
A value matching this type is valid if it matches *any* member type.

intersection type.description:
TS 1.6
type Name = A & B
A value matching this type must satisfy *all* member types simultaneously — commonly used to combine object shapes.

tuple type.description:
TS 1.0 (labels: TS 4.0; optional/variadic elements: TS 3.0/4.0)
type Name = [label: Type, ...]
A fixed-length (or partially fixed) array with a known type per position; elements can be labeled, optional (`?`), or a variadic rest element.

readonly array / tuple.description:
TS 3.4
readonly T[] | ReadonlyArray<T>
An array/tuple type whose mutating methods (`push`, `splice`, index assignment, ...) are removed at the type level.

index signature.description:
TS 1.0
index signature
Describes an object whose property keys aren't known ahead of time but whose key/value types are.

function type expression.description:
TS 1.0
type Name = (arg: T) => R
Describes the shape of a callable value — parameter and return types only, no implementation.

call & construct signature.description:
TS 1.0
call signature / construct signature
Describes a value that can be invoked directly (call signature) and/or with `new` (construct signature) — e.g. typing a class constructor value.

unknown type.description:
TS 3.0
unknown
The type-safe counterpart of `any` — accepts anything, but must be narrowed (`typeof`, `instanceof`, a type guard) before use. Prefer over `any` at API boundaries.

never type.description:
TS 2.0
never
The type of a value that never occurs — a function that always throws, or an exhaustiveness-check branch that should be unreachable.

as const object literal.description:
TS 3.4
const Name = { ... } as const
A plain object literal frozen to its most specific (readonly, literal) type. The community- and TypeScript-team-recommended alternative to `enum`: enums generate real runtime code and are excluded from the `erasableSyntaxOnly` (TS 5.8+) type-stripping model that Node.js/Deno/Bun use to run `.ts` files directly — `as const` objects are plain JS and need no such carve-out.
